To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

brimonidine tartrate (Alphagan P; Alcon Laboratories, Inc.) is effective for decreasing intraocular pressure (IOP) after argon laser trabeculopathy (ALT), that the efficacy of brimonide is similar to that of dorzolamide (Cosopt; Merck & Co, Inc.) and that the efficacy is greater than that of timolol maleate (TIM; Timoptic; Alcon).

1) the efficacy of brimonidin in decreasing intraocular pressure after ALT was comparable to the efficacy of timolol, but the duration of the effect was shorter, 2) the efficacy of ALT in lowering intraocular pressure was comparable to that of timolol in patients with POAG, and 3) the combination of ALT and brimonidine was more effective than ALT alone in patients with POA.

1) brimonidine 0.2% ophthalmic solution was as effective as timolol 0.5% ophthalmic suspension at reducing the intraocular pressure (IOP) after laser trabecuoplasty; 2) the incidence of adverse events was low in both treatment groups; and 3) brimonidine was more effective than timolol at reducing the IOP in patients with a baseline IOP of 21 to 25 mmHg
